references.text: God had already promised to give Midian into Gideon's hand, and the dream confirms this promise
Gideon understands the meaning of the dream and worships God before going out to attack the Midianites
The fulfillment of the dream: The Lord turned the swords of the Midianites against each other
Gideon is first introduced as the son of Joash from Ophrah, who is mentioned in the interpretation of the dream
The Lord's original call to Gideon to save Israel from Midian
The final victory over Midian and their entire camp, just as the dream predicted
The psalm mentions the victory over Midian and their leaders as an example of God's mighty deeds
Isaiah refers to 'the day of Midian' as a picture of God's deliverance and victory
The prophet compares God's coming judgment with the victory over Midian at the rock of Oreb
